key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow makes it possible to map phase stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloys and shows that the Sn-based alloys are less stable than the Pb-based ones, especially away from iodine-rich compositions.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a practical composition guide for designing more stable perovskite solar absorbers and narrow the search space for alloy engineering in Pb- and Sn-based systems.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data for fast structure relaxation
Secondary ML models that predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures
Free-energy landscape calculations across composition and phase space, including disorder and FA orientation
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated by generating free-energy landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 across compositions and phases, revealing stable regions and their dependence on iodide content.
watch_item: The workflow is computationally powerful but depends on the quality and coverage of the DFT training data, so predictions may be less reliable outside the sampled composition and structural space.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
